task.name: Models this project validated are reachable only from project configuration, so a consumer starting from shipped defaults does not get them
task.story_text:
## Why

The shipped model catalog now loads from data, and adding a model to it no longer requires a
release. The catalog's contents were migrated faithfully from the previous hardcoded set, which was
the right scope for that change — but it means the catalog reflects what was hardcoded historically
rather than what this project has since validated and run.

Three models this project routes to daily exist only as project-level declarations: a strong-tier
OpenAI entry, a Google entry adopted after its predecessor was benched, and an Anthropic cheap-tier
entry. Each was chosen deliberately, each has run in production sprints, and each is reachable only
by a consumer who declares it themselves. A repository installing this project and enabling the
shipped defaults gets a catalog whose newest OpenAI tier is a generation behind what this project
runs, and no cheap-tier Anthropic option at all — despite that model already being billed inside
invocations as a component.

The declarations already exist and already carry their routing policy and cost seeds. What is
missing is that they live in the consumer-invisible half of the configuration.

## Acceptance criteria

- A repository that installs this project and enables the shipped defaults resolves the models this
  project routes to, without declaring any of them itself.
- A model that has been validated for general use is reachable from the shipped catalog rather than
  only from a project-level declaration.
- Each promoted entry carries the routing policy and cost seeds it was validated under, so
  promotion moves a definition rather than restating it from memory.
- Where the same canonical identity is defined both in the shipped catalog and in project
  configuration, resolution states which source supplies each field and which one wins. A duplicate
  declaration is not assumed to be inert: pricing attribution differs by source, and attribution
  participates in routing, so the resolved entry must record where its figures came from.
- An operator who removes a duplicate declaration gets the same routing behaviour as one who keeps
  it, or the difference is reported rather than silent.
- This change does not modify the project's own configuration file. Removing the now-redundant
  declarations is separate operator work, sequenced after a release containing these catalog entries
  has been deployed — the process that runs sprints reads an installed release, and a configuration
  that drops its declarations before that release exists would reference models the deployed catalog
  cannot resolve, failing config load and preventing any sprint from starting.
- A model whose identifier has not been confirmed against its provider is not added, so the catalog
  does not acquire entries that fail at dispatch.

## Example

What the two halves contain today:

```
shipped catalog        anthropic/sonnet/cli   anthropic/opus/cli
(data/models.yaml)     openai/gpt-5.4/cli     openai/gpt-5.4-mini/cli   ...

project-only           openai/gpt-5.5/cli            strong tier, in daily use
(forge.yaml)           google/gemini-3.5-flash/api   adopted after its predecessor was benched
                       anthropic/haiku/cli           cheap tier; already billed as a component model
```

After promotion the second group is reachable from the first, and the project's own configuration
drops roughly twenty-six lines of declaration that exist only to restate them.

handoff.summary: Kept the prior commit's catalog promotion (openai/gpt-5.5/cli, google/gemini-3.5-flash/api, anthropic/haiku/cli in config/data/models.yaml with the routing policy and cost seeds they were validated under) and reworked duplicate resolution to match the revised AC4/AC5. Measured that a duplicate declaration is NOT inert: anthropic/haiku/cli's price tie-break signal is 5.0 with the forge.yaml declaration and inf without it, because the shipped entry is an unattributed vendor shorthand, so removing the declaration would change cheap-tier selection; the other two differ only in attribution label and route identically. Added src/theforge/config/model_duplicates.py (new module: model_catalog.py is at 599 lines against the hard 600 cap) computing the comparison and splitting routing differences (tier/capability/cost_rank/dev_capable/phase_eligibility/base_url plus the attribution-gated effective_*_cost_per_mtok) from attribution differences (pricing_provenance/cost_rank_basis/raw price literals). Scoped the models.custom duplicate guard to duplicates that actually change routing so promotion cannot break a config that already matched the entry, recorded every duplicate on ForgeConfig.model_registry_duplicates (which puts it in the resolved-config digest), warn via the theforge.config logger at load, and added a check-config section stating per duplicate which source wins, which fields differ, and whether it is safe to remove. forge.yaml is untouched.

acceptance_criteria.notes: All three resolve from load_packaged_catalog(); covered by a config that selects them with no custom/inline declaration and asserts model_registry_sources == builtin and zero duplicates.

acceptance_criteria.notes: All three are in data/models.yaml, hence AGENT_REGISTRY. Also pinned as properties: newest OpenAI CLI tier includes gpt-5.5, and a cheap-tier Anthropic entry now exists.

acceptance_criteria.notes: model_registry_field_sources already gives per-field provenance; added model_registry_duplicates recording, per duplicate, every differing field with both sides' values, split into routing vs attribution. is_redundant is only true when nothing differs at all, so an attribution-only duplicate is reported rather than equated. check-config prints 'also defined in the shipped catalog (forge.yaml wins)' with the field-level detail.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An operator who removes a duplicate declaration gets the same routing behaviour as one who keeps it, or the difference is reported rather than silent.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Both branches exercised. Attribution-only duplicates: seam test asserts derive_roles picks (dev/preflight/plan/review pool) are identical with and without the declaration. haiku genuinely differs, so it is reported: a logger warning at load, a check-config WARNINGS entry, and a 'ROUTING DIFFERS — removing it changes model selection' line. A seam test pins the underlying tie-break move (inf vs 5.0).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: This change does not modify the project's own configuration file.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Verified by git diff HEAD -- forge.yaml (empty). The guard is scoped to routing-changing duplicates precisely so forge.yaml keeps loading unmodified once the release ships; confirmed by loading the real forge.yaml.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A model whose identifier has not been confirmed against its provider is not added, so the catalog does not acquire entries that fail at dispatch.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Only the three verified identities were promoted. The BLOCKED gpt-5.6 family (temperature bug, unconfirmed Codex CLI support) was excluded, guarded by a test asserting no gpt-5.6* model is in the registry.

story_deviations: Touched more than data/models.yaml (which preflight expected to be the only file): added config/model_duplicates.py and changed load.py, types.py, and cli/check_config.py. Required by AC4/AC5 — preflight assessed the existing per-field provenance machinery as already satisfying AC4, but it does not answer whether a duplicate changes routing, and nothing reported that. The models.custom guard also raised outright on this project's own declarations once their identities became builtin, which would have violated the do-not-modify-forge.yaml sequencing AC.

Modified tests/test_invocation_ledger.py, which asserted claude-haiku-4-5 resolves as 'unresolved' because the catalog did not know it — the exact premise this story removes (the spec cites haiku as 'already billed inside invocations as a component' while 'absent from the catalog entirely'). Updated to assert 'canonical' plus the canonical id; the unresolved path stays covered by test_divergence_falls_back_to_raw_spellings_when_neither_canonicalizes.

Earlier in the branch, tests/test_pricing_provenance.py (haiku added to the CLI-shorthand unattributed set) and tests/test_profiles_migration.py (family-match example moved off haiku to an identifier with no registry slot) were updated for the same reason.
deferred_items: Removing the three now-redundant declarations from forge.yaml is operator work, explicitly sequenced after a release carrying these catalog entries is deployed. Note when doing so: dropping anthropic/haiku/cli is NOT behaviour-neutral — it moves haiku's price tie-break signal from 5.0 to inf (shipped entry is an unattributed vendor shorthand), so cheap-tier selection can change. check-config now states this per duplicate.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
